\section{Overview}

\section{Declarations}

\begin{lemma}[Real Exponent Form of the Hypercontractive Condition]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hypercontractive_toReal_condition}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hypercontractive_toReal_condition}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
Let $p,q\in[0,\infty]$ and $\rho\in\mathbb R$. If $1\le p\le q$, $q$ is finite, and
$\rho^2(q-1)\le p-1$ in the extended nonnegative reals, then $\rho^2(q-1)\le p-1$ as an
inequality of real numbers.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Nonzero Correlation Forces Finite Exponents]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hypercontractive_exponents_of_nonzero}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hypercontractive_exponents_of_nonzero}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hypercontractive_toReal_condition}
\difficulty{5}
Let $p,q\in[0,\infty]$, let $\rho\in\mathbb R$ be nonzero, and suppose $1\le p<q$ and
$\rho^2(q-1)\le p-1$, with the inequality interpreted in the extended nonnegative reals.
Then $1<p$ and $q$ is finite.
\end{lemma}
